title: Tiananmen Square massacre: Le Monde reveals unseen footage of the Chinese regime's violent repression
subhead: Art historian Nathalie Trouveroy shared footage from her personal archives of the Tiananmen Square protests with Le Monde, shedding new light on how the Chinese regime violently repressed the student protests in June 1989.

title: Analysis: France's Constitutional Council dispels questions about assisted-dying law and strengthens 'conscience clauses'
subhead: The Council supported patients' 'personal freedom' to access a lethal substance at their request, if approved by a doctor. It granted private and nonprofit institutions the right to refuse aid-in-dying procedures on their premises.

title: 'Like House of Cards': Infantino's opponents make moves to unseat FIFA president
subhead: According to a working document seen by Le Monde, UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC want to change FIFA's presidency into a rotating, representative and ceremonial role with a 'fixed two-year term,' modeled on the Swiss Confederation.

title: Mortality during heatwaves: Key housing, inequality and hospital factors remain overlooked
subhead: The French government has focused its heatwave messaging on individual actions, preventative measures, and vigilance, but failed to emphasize several central issues that are vital to tackling the heat's most severe health impacts.

subhead: Some 12 million people live alone in France, and their number continues to rise. The country's housing stock has not kept pace with this trend, exacerbating the impact of the housing crisis on these individuals.

title: 'I'll pay for a breast. Even both, if you want': The costs, big and small, of breast surgery in the private sector
subhead: 'My Breasts and Me' (5/5). In France, one out of every two patients chooses the private sector for breast reconstruction. Some are willing to give up their vacations, take out a loan or turn to their parents for help. Le Monde spent several weeks inside a private breast surgery practice in Paris.

title: 'It was either exile or prison': An interview with Boris Nadezhdin, Putin opponent who fled to France
subhead: The veteran Russian politician, 63, tried to challenge Vladimir Putin's regime and its war in Ukraine through legal and electoral means. He failed. Facing the threat of arrest, he decided to leave Russia. His interview with Le Monde is his first since arriving in France.
